ordered_diagnoses: Central retinal artery occlusion due to cancer-associated thrombosis

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss in one eye with optic disc swelling and retinal vascular occlusion
salient_findings: Sudden vision loss in the right eye
Marked swelling of the optic disc
Peripapillary retinal hemorrhages
Occlusion of the superior branch artery
Combined occlusion of the central retinal artery and vein
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 40s
Presented with blurred vision in the right eye
Undergoing treatment with systemic steroids, durvalumab, and bevacizumab
Initial visual acuity was 20/25 OU
Right eye had full visual field and relative afferent pupillary defect
Mild swelling of the optic disc on initial examination
Normal fundus and visual function in the left eye
Vision loss occurred 10 days after initial presentation
MRI showed focal enhancement along enlarged right optic nerve
Lumbar puncture showed no abnormalities
Vitreous biopsy showed hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm

shortlist: Central retinal artery occlusion due to cancer-associated thrombosis

shortlist.label: Neoplastic optic neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Vitreous biopsy showed hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm

shortlist.label: Lymphomatous optic neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is undergoing treatment with systemic steroids, durvalumab, and bevacizumab, which may increase the risk of lymphoma

shortlist.label: Intraocular lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Vitreous biopsy showed hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm, which could be related to lymphoma

shortlist.label: Optic nerve sheath meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: MRI showed focal enhancement along enlarged right optic nerve, which could be consistent with a meningioma

shortlist.label: Central retinal artery occlusion due to cancer-associated thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of cancer treatment and developed sudden vision loss, which could be related to cancer-associated thrombosis

raw.rationale: The presence of a hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm in the vitreous biopsy, along with the patient's history of sudden vision loss and the imaging findings, supports the diagnosis of intraocular lymphoma. The positive immunohistochemistry results for glial fibrillary acid protein and other markers also point towards a neoplastic process.

rejected.label: Neoplastic optic neuropathy
rejected.why: While the patient has a neoplastic process, the involvement of the vitreous and the specific findings suggest a more specific diagnosis of intraocular lymphoma.

rejected.label: Lymphomatous optic neuropathy
rejected.why: The biopsy results and the clinical presentation are more consistent with intraocular lymphoma than lymphomatous optic neuropathy, which typically involves the optic nerve itself.

rejected.label: Optic nerve sheath meningioma
rejected.why: The imaging findings and biopsy results do not support a diagnosis of optic nerve sheath meningioma, which would typically show a distinct mass involving the optic nerve sheath.

rejected.label: Central retinal artery occlusion due to cancer-associated thrombosis
rejected.why: While the patient did experience central retinal artery occlusion, the underlying cause appears to be related to the intraocular lymphoma rather than a primary thrombotic event.
